newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soccer-Venables urges World Cup caution.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Venables urges World Cup caution.

text.p: National soccer coach Terry Venables has warned against complacency over Australia's World Cup prospects, saying it's ridiculous to assume his side are certain of qualifying for next year's finals.
Australia must win the Oceania qualifying group and then beat an Asian team in a play-off to reach the finals in France.
Traditional rivals New Zealand will provide the only genuine challenge in the Oceania qualifiers, which will be held in June.
"To say that we have easier (qualifying) games in the beginning than the end is stating the obvious," Venables said.
"But anyone we play in Asia -- if we get to that stage -- is going to be difficult," the former England coach said.
Venables has arrived in Australia for a two-match Gold v Green trial matches, starting in Melbourne on May 28. He will use the games as a final form check before naming his squad.

Several overseas-based players, including Lazio midfielder Paul Okon, Middlesborough goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer and Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder Steve Corica will be missing from the two-match series becuase of injury.
Defender Kevin Muscat will be absent for the first match because he is needed by Crystal Palace for their English First Division promotion play-off.

"The Superstars games are perfect for the Australian-based players, coming at the end of the domestic season, but we always knew there would be a problem with some of the European-based players," Venables said.
Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich and Tenerife striker Aurelio Vidmar will head the overseas contingent.
